messages:
Mike Chen: Heads up — AtlasHealth pulled forward their Dedicated contract conversation for Q3. They want a 24/7 committed throughput floor (chat workloads, ~512 token avg). Rough ask: steady baseline plus headroom for bursty clinic hours. Can infra ops recommend a floor and a burst policy?
Priya Rao: Quick facts we need: daily tokens estimate, p95 concurrency, target p99 latency SLO. do we have their sample traces?
Mike Chen: They sent an anonymized trace: ~18M tokens/day, median convo length ~6 turns. No p95 yet. Asking us to propose a commit (not final pricing) — they expect a predictable monthly unit.
Ashley M: From finance: we need to map any proposed GPU-reserve to monthly committed spend tiers. If we under-commit we lose margin; if we over-commit we risk customer churn. please include a low/mid/high cost scenario. :chart_with_upwards_trend:
Omar A: Quick napkin: 18M tokens/day ~= 208 tokens/sec avg. For 512-token prompts that’s ~0.4 requests/sec average. But clinic peaks around 10x average. So design for 2k tokens/sec sustained with 10k tokens/sec burst headroom?
Lucy Park: Agree on modelling peaks. Also region split: they want EU primary (eu-west), US fallback. That means reserve in both regions or rely on routing fallback. Latency-sensitive requests should be in eu-west. We should propose a primary reserved pool in eu-west and a small standby in us-west for failover/burst.
Priya Rao: Ops question: how many vGPU equivalents is that? Can we surface a simple conversion table in the proposal so sales can pick a commit band?
DevOps Bot: Capacity snapshot: eu-west reserved headroom = 6 A100-equivalent GPUs available in the next 60d window; us-west reserved headroom = 3 A100-equivalent. Current fleet utilization: 72% eu-west, 63% us-west.
Jon S: For sizing, I prefer a model that uses 3 buckets: floor (SLA-backed), buffer (guaranteed but lower SLA), burst (best effort). Example: floor = 40% of 24/7 18M tokens/day demand, buffer = +40%, burst = +20% on top for clinic peaks. That gives us predictable billing tiers.
Ashley M: Can you translate that to monthly committed GPU-hours? We need a dollar estimate to show them.
Omar A: I'll run the conversion. Plan: convert tokens/day -> tokens/sec -> average model throughput per GPU at our standard profiling conditions -> add safety multiplier 1.6 for p95 and quantization variance.
Priya Rao: Useful quick query (run in BigQuery billing dataset):
```
SELECT service, SUM(cost) as cost FROM `billing.gcp_*` WHERE sku_description LIKE '%A100%' AND DATE(_PARTITIONTIME) BETWEEN DATE_SUB(CURRENT_DATE(), INTERVAL 90 DAY) AND CURRENT_DATE() GROUP BY service;
```
This gives us a regional spend baseline to propose discount tiers.
Lucy Park: Also include network egress risk: eu->us failover traffic could spike egress costs. Flagging to finance.
Mike Chen: Proposed next steps: 1) Omar to produce three commit bands (floor/buffer/burst -> gpu-equivalents + monthly $) by EOD tomorrow. 2) Priya to sanity-check model perf numbers with ML infra. 3) Lucy to call out region/failover egress estimate. 4) Ashley to draft pricing bands.
Omar A: On it — will attach the perf assumptions and a short calc table.
Jon S: If we can, include an option with elastic burst credits (like a burst bucket charged at premium) so the customer can avoid big upfront commit but still have safety.
Ashley M: That productized burst credit idea is viable but needs legal ops for contract language. Adding to tracker. :page_with_curl:
Priya Rao: One more item — make sure we show historical utilization trend for the last 3 months (daily tokens and 95th percentile). Sales likes visuals but a simple CSV is fine.
Mike Chen: Great. If we can get a crisp commit proposal (3 bands + burst credit option + egress warning) we can present on Friday. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
DevOps Bot: Ticket created: DEDICATED-COMMIT-1805002001 (assignees: Omar A, Priya Rao, Lucy Park, Ashley M)
